prompt:
Paint a transparent-background pixel-art atlas of exactly FOUR candidate views of one Personal Space NE plaster-and-timber wall: four columns, one row, ordered RIGHT, LEFT, TOP, BOTTOM. The left panel in the reference sheet is the sole target identity/material source: a narrow warm-orange timber end face with pale cream plaster, dark outline, and one diagonal timber brace. The right panel is a same-kit NORTHWEST broad wall shape guide ONLY; do not copy its exact pixels or reverse its identity. Repaint the broad views using the NE target's materials, frame style, and diagonal brace.

This wall has a long world-Y axis, narrow world-X thickness, and upright world-Z height. RIGHT and LEFT are the two true broad long Y/Z elevations, matching the broad rectangular horizontal wall span of the same-kit geometry guide. Each should be a wide, level, rectangular plaster face with warm orange timber outer posts/top/bottom rails and one dark-edged diagonal orange brace in the plaster; opposite camera may show the brace reversed, but keep one brace only. Both side elevations must share the SAME full Z height and broad Y span as one another, not short thin posts. TOP and BOTTOM are directly overhead/underfoot, not wall elevations: each is a long thin world-Y wood-frame strip, with the narrow depth of the wall, top cap timber and long continuous wood/plaster-edge surfaces; no full-height upright post or broad front face. Match plan length to the broad elevation Y span. Keep lines and materials from the target NE end face; hidden surfaces are inferred conservatively.

Only four cells, one object per cell. The RIGHT and LEFT views must be broad horizontal wall faces; TOP/BOTTOM must be thin long horizontal footprints. Axis-aligned orthographic cameras, no perspective/isometric. Transparent background, crisp pixels, strong dark outline, one common object scale, no clipping, no scene or text.
